items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.2.4 at source lines 730-742: the cardinal numbers form a commutative semiring, with all seven displayed laws. The author's proof (source lines 743-750) proves multiplication commutativity and declares the rest analogous, but the proof of that one law is a chain of reductions that consumes three separate facts: because card is a set the goal is a mere proposition, so induction reduces it to cardinals of sets (lines 745-746); the definitions of the operations then rewrite the goal as an identity between cd(A x B) and cd(B x A) (line 747); and univalence turns that identity into the requirement of an equivalence between the products, which is supplied by the swapping map (lines 748-749). The statement lists the seven laws and hides that the reduction passes through truncation induction, definitional unfolding and univalence.
